newsitem.title: JAPAN: Rubber - Japan market seen easing on supply concerns.
newsitem.headline: Rubber - Japan market seen easing on supply concerns.

text.p: Japanese rubber futures are likely to ease as expectations of a large number of deliveries at the spot expiry later this month are growing, given a sharp rise in Japan's rubber stocks, traders said on Monday.
"Sentiment remains bearish. There could be as much as 1,300 lots of deliveries at the spot expiry, considering a recent gain in rubber stocks," an analyst at a commodity broker said.
"The market will ease, led by nearby months. Market participants are watching for when the nearby months stop falling," the analyst said.
"In line with the weakness in nearby months, the benchmark February on TOCOM could test the low of 135.4 yen marked on August 12," the analyst said.
But some traders said the market could post a moderate technical rebound as caution over oversold conditions is likely to emerge after recent price falls.
The benchmark February contract on the Tokyo Commodity Exchange ended the Monday morning session at 138.3 yen, down from 139.7 yen last Friday.
Benchmark February on Kobe Rubber Exchange was 138.6 yen in the morning session, down from 139.3 yen on Friday.
Japan's rubber stocks at designated warehouses rose to 41,869 tonnes as of August 31, up about 48 percent from the end of July, according to the Rubber Trade Association of Japan.
It is the first time natural rubber stocks have broken above 40,000 tonnes since April 1993, it said.
Traders said stocks were likely to rise further, probably to 50,000 tonnes by October, casting a shadow over the rubber futures markets.
Compared with nearby months, any price losses in distant months could be limited, supported by possible trading house buying.
The Thai benchmark rubber offer price to Japan was quoted at 127.50 cents as of Monday, down 1.50 cents from last Friday.

"Bearing in mind rain in producing countries, offer prices from Thailand have not fallen enough, which has made Japanese traders wary of buying rubber in producing countries," a trader said. They were instead buying distant months for hedging.

In Japan's physical market, prices of Thai rubber ribbed smoked sheet (RSS) 3 to large-lot end-users fell to 147 yen per kg last Friday due to oversupply fears in the near term, down from 153 yen at the end of August.
